how_graded: Each output in results/outputs_gpu.json read by hand against the expected answer in prompts.json. The palindrome functions (prompt 3) were executed against 5 test strings, all passed.

per_prompt.1 arithmetic (16): all correct; q4 drops the LaTeX formatting, same working
per_prompt.3 code: all correct, same function; all ignore 'only output the code' and add test prints; q4 picks different test cases
per_prompt.5 logic (yes): all correct; q4 gives a 94-token explanation instead of ~30
per_prompt.6 summary: all one accurate sentence, worded slightly differently
per_prompt.7 translation: all identical; 'se clôture' is understandable but unidiomatic ('ferme' is the natural verb)
per_prompt.10 miles to km (8.05): all correct; q8 adds a 115-token worked calculation, fp16 and q4 answer in one line

observations: Quality. All three precisions answered all 10 prompts correctly; the generated code passed 5 test strings in every case. Differences are only in style and length: with greedy decoding, q8_0 reproduced the fp16 text exactly on 7/10 prompts and q4_K_M on 6/10 (mean character similarity to fp16 0.86 / 0.87). Where they diverge, the quantised model takes a different but equally valid path (q8 writes a long worked calculation for the unit conversion, q4 a longer logic explanation and different test cases), because a small change in the logits flips one early token and greedy decoding then follows a different continuation. Shared weaknesses are model-level, not precision-level: all three use the unidiomatic 'se clôture' and ignore 'only output the code'. One more effect: CPU and GPU runs of the same quantised file were identical on only 7/10 (q8) and 5/10 (q4) prompts versus 10/10 for fp16, since the two backends dequantise and accumulate in a different order. Speed and memory. fp16 does not fit a 4 GB laptop GPU next to the desktop's own usage: Ollama put 64% of it in VRAM and ran the rest on the CPU, and the CPU half sets the pace (9.7 tok/s). q8_0 and q4_K_M fit entirely and run 8x and 10x faster. On CPU only, speed tracks bytes per weight almost exactly (3.9 → 7.8 → 13.9 tok/s for 16 → 8.5 → ~4.8 bits), which is what you expect when decoding is limited by memory bandwidth.
prompt_table_note: Prompts (prompts.json): arithmetic word problem, capital of Australia, palindrome function, JSON extraction, syllogism, one-sentence summary, English→French, count r in 'strawberry', 17 x 24, miles→km. Full outputs: task3-local-inference/results/outputs_gpu.json (and outputs_cpu.json).
